sections.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: Why are the early years called the formative years?
questions.answer: Because the foundation for physical, cognitive, socio-emotional and language development is laid in this period.

questions.q: How much of brain development is complete by the age of six?
Name any two factors that lead to developmental delays.
questions.answer: Any two: an unhealthy home or school environment, too little stimulation, inadequate nutrition, poor health care.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: ECCE is an ________ programme with several components.
questions.answer: integrated

questions.q: Name any two components of ECCE.
questions.answer: Any two: health, nutrition and hygiene; care and protection; early stimulation; early learning.

questions.q: How does quality ECCE help a child later in school?
questions.answer: The child gains age-appropriate knowledge and skills and adjusts better to the formal school environment.

sections.passage: Early childhood refers to the early years of life from birth to six years. These years are called the formative years as the foundation for physical, cognitive, socio-emotional and language development is laid during this period. Research in neuroscience shows that by the time a child is six years old, 90% of brain development has taken place. Lack of a healthy home and school environment, too little stimulation, inadequate nutrition and poor health care are common factors that lead to developmental delays. ECCE is an integrated programme whose components — health, nutrition and hygiene; care and protection; early stimulation; and early learning — together contribute to the development and wellbeing of children. Quality ECCE helps children acquire age-appropriate knowledge and skills and adjust better in a formal school environment.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (match the columns, true/false, fill in the blanks or one-word answers).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) According to research in neuroscience, 90% of brain development has occurred by the time a child reaches six years. (ii) Lack of a healthy home and school environment can contribute to developmental delays in children.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True.
questions.note: April 2025 asked the 90% figure as an MCQ.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) ECCE means ensuring health and nutrition only. (ii) Home and school environment do not affect the development of children.
questions.answer: (i) False — ECCE includes care, health, nutrition and early learning. (ii) False — a poor home and school environment can delay development.
questions.note: The same question had: 'Early years of children's life are very important due to fast growth and development in all domains' — True.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Quality early care and education provided through ECCE programmes helps children adjust better in a formal school environment. (ii) ECCE primarily focuses on the care of children aged three to six years.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False — ECCE covers children from birth to six years.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) The Montessori method is primarily focused on elementary education. (ii) Mahatma Gandhi, Rabindranath Tagore and Zakir Hussain stressed that education should be imparted in the children's mother tongue.
questions.answer: (i) False — it is an approach to preschool education. (ii) True.

questions.q: Answer in one word or phrase: (i) What is the aim of ECCE? (ii) What does 'early stimulation' refer to?
questions.answer: (i) Holistic (overall) development of all children in their formative years. (ii) Stimulating inputs through the five senses — seeing, hearing, touching, smelling and tasting — in the first years of life.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Gijubhai Badheka founded Bal Mandir in ________, Gujarat in 1920. (ii) Sustainable Development Goal ________ targets that by 2030 all girls and boys have access to quality early childhood development, care and pre-primary education.
questions.answer: (i) Bhavnagar (ii) 4 (target 4.2)

questions.q: Match: (a) ICDS scheme (b) UN Convention on the Rights of the Child — (i) 1989 (ii) 1975 (iii) 2013

Fill in the blanks: (i) Physical-motor development involves the development of gross and fine muscles and ________ coordination. (ii) Language development involves the skills of listening, speaking, reading and ________.
questions.answer: (i) eye-hand (ii) writing

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is the objective of ECCE? Write any two objectives.
questions.answer: ECCE aims to provide quality care and learning opportunities to all children in their formative years for their overall development. Objectives (any two): children feel safe, secure, accepted and respected; good, balanced nutrition; healthy habits, hygiene and self-help skills; sound language and communication; physical-motor development; sensory and cognitive abilities; social competence and emotional wellbeing; readiness for formal schooling.

questions.q: Why are the first six years of life considered crucial for development?
questions.answer: They are a time of very fast growth and development in all domains, and 90% of brain development takes place by six. Any deprivation then (poor nutrition, health care or stimulation) can cause developmental delays, while quality care and early learning lay the base for later learning.
questions.note: October 2024 asked this as an MCQ ('time for rapid development').

questions.q: What is meant by developmental delay? Give two causes.
questions.answer: Developmental delay means a child does not reach the developmental milestones (age-specific skills) at the expected age and lags behind the normal pattern. Causes (any two): heredity, complications during pregnancy or childbirth, illness, accidents after birth, poor nutrition or stimulation.

questions.q: What do you understand by the 'components of ECCE'? Name them.
questions.answer: ECCE is an integrated programme whose parts together support children's development and wellbeing. Its components are: health, nutrition and hygiene; care and protection; early stimulation; and early learning.

questions.q: What were the contributions of Gijubhai Badheka and Tarabai Modak to preschool education in India?
questions.answer: Gijubhai Badheka believed good education is vital for proper development and founded Bal Mandir, a preschool, in Bhavnagar, Gujarat in 1920. Tarabai Modak founded the Nutan Bal Shikshan Sangh in Bombay (Mumbai) in 1926, where children of different backgrounds learnt through activities and real-life experiences.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the meaning of the term ECCE.
questions.answer: ECCE has three key terms. Early childhood is the period from birth to six years (sub-stages: conception to birth, birth to three, three to six). Care means love, affection and a healthy, hygienic, protective and stimulating environment. Education is acquiring knowledge, skills, attitudes and values through exploration, experimentation, observation, participation and interaction. So ECCE means providing care — including health and nutrition — and early learning opportunities to all young children through play-based, developmentally appropriate activities for their holistic development.

or.q: Discuss the key components of ECCE.
or.answer: Health, nutrition and hygiene: care of the mother before and after birth (nutritious food, immunisation, check-ups, safe delivery) and of the child (balanced diet, protection from infection, immunisation, medical care). Care and protection: a physically and emotionally safe environment with warm, responsive interaction. Early stimulation: inputs through the five senses in the first three years, which build neural pathways. Early learning: play, concrete experiences, observation, manipulation and experimentation for children of three to six.

questions.q: What is the significance of discussing ECCE with parents in the community?
questions.answer: Many parents do not know how important the first six years are, when 90% of the brain develops. Discussing ECCE makes them aware of nutrition, health care, immunisation and stimulation at home; encourages them to send children to an anganwadi or preschool; helps them avoid formal teaching of the 3Rs too early; and builds a partnership between home and centre, so delays are noticed early and children develop holistically.

or.q: How does ECCE contribute to preparing children for formal learning in schools?
or.answer: ECCE gives children age-appropriate knowledge and skills through play: language and communication, early concepts (colour, shape, number), fine motor control for writing, self-help skills, and social skills such as sharing and following routines. It also builds attention, curiosity and confidence. So children adjust better to the formal school environment, which is one of the stated objectives of ECCE.

questions.q: What is early intervention? Why is it important?
questions.answer: Early intervention means taking necessary action as early as possible on a child's developmental and learning needs to reduce the effects of a delay. It matters because the young mind is most receptive then; delays not addressed in time may become permanent and later help may not be enough to catch up. Regular check-ups and health records help detect problems such as a hearing difficulty early, so they can be treated at once.

questions.q: Briefly describe ECCE in the global context.
questions.answer: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) protects children's survival, health, education and protection. The World Conference on Education for All, Jomtien, Thailand (1990) said 'learning begins at birth' and called for early care and education with family and community involvement. The World Education Forum, Dakar (2000) set Education For All goals, and the Forum at Incheon, Korea (2015) led to SDG 4: by 2030 all girls and boys should have quality early childhood development, care and pre-primary education.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the term ECCE. Which objectives of ECCE would you give priority to in an urban context?
questions.answer: ECCE means providing care — love, a healthy, hygienic, protective and stimulating environment, health and nutrition — together with early learning opportunities to all children from birth to six years, through play-based, developmentally appropriate activities for holistic development. In an urban setting, where both parents often work and families are small: (1) children should feel safe, secure, accepted and respected in crèches and preschools; (2) good, balanced nutrition, as fast food and irregular meals are common; (3) healthy habits, hygiene and self-help skills; (4) physical-motor development through outdoor play, since space is limited and screen time high; (5) pro-social skills and emotional wellbeing, as children have fewer playmates at home; (6) language and communication; and (7) readiness for formal school without pushing early academics.

or.q: What are the different components of ECCE? Discuss any two that are most important for a child's survival.
or.answer: The components are health, nutrition and hygiene; care and protection; early stimulation; and early learning. Most important for survival: (1) Health, nutrition and hygiene — prenatal and postnatal care of the mother (nutritious food, immunisation, check-ups, safe delivery in a hospital) and for the child a balanced diet, breastfeeding, protection from infection, timely immunisation and medical care; these reduce infant and child deaths. (2) Care and protection — a physically and emotionally safe, secure environment, warm responsive caregivers and protection from harm and neglect, so the child's psychological and physical needs are met.

questions.note: April 2023 asked: explain the meaning of ECCE and describe its objectives.

questions.q: Why is ECCE important for children? Describe ECCE in the Indian context.
questions.answer: Importance: the first six years see the fastest growth in all domains and 90% of brain development; deprivation of nutrition, health care or stimulation causes delays, while quality ECCE gives age-appropriate skills, holistic development and better adjustment to school. Indian context: pioneers Gijubhai Badheka (Bal Mandir, Bhavnagar, 1920), Tarabai Modak (Nutan Bal Shikshan Sangh, Bombay, 1926) and the Montessori Method; thinkers Gandhi, Tagore and Zakir Hussain wanted education in the mother tongue linked to the child's culture. The Government launched ICDS in 1975 for the health, nutrition and development of children under six and for pregnant and lactating mothers; Five Year Plans and the National ECCE Policy, 2013 widened access. ECCE is delivered by public, private (nurseries, kindergartens, pre-primary sections) and NGO providers.
